analysis.investment_thesis: Manoj Jewellers fails the Magic Formula's "good business" test decisively — a 0.39% ROE signals capital is earning almost nothing, regardless of the optically cheap 4.96x P/E. A cheap bad business is still a bad business; the Magic Formula requires BOTH cheap AND high-quality, and this is a micro-cap jeweller with neither moat nor returns on capital.
key_strengths: P/E of 4.96 suggests a high headline earnings yield (~20%)
Promoter holding of 65.28% indicates aligned skin-in-the-game
Small Rs 40.4 Cr market cap leaves theoretical room for re-rating if operations scale
key_risks: ROE of 0.39% implies ROIC is near zero — fails the Magic Formula quality filter
Jewellery retail is capital-intensive (gold inventory) with razor-thin margins and no moat
Micro-cap with minimal institutional oversight (DII 0%) and likely illiquid
red_flags: ROE of 0.39% is effectively sub-treasury-bill returns on equity
Low P/E may reflect one-time income or distressed earnings, not durable cash flow
No disclosed EBIT or capital employed data to verify Magic Formula metrics cleanly
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on two dimensions: earnings yield (cheapness) and return on capital (quality). Manoj Jewellers may score acceptably on the first — a 4.96 P/E implies an earnings yield near 20% before EV adjustments — but it catastrophically fails the second. An ROE of 0.39% is a near-zero return on shareholder capital, which mathematically forces ROIC to also be trivial. In my framework, ROIC below 12% is a red flag; below 1% is disqualifying. You're paying a "cheap" multiple for a business that produces almost no economic profit.

Jewellery retail in India is structurally difficult: high working capital locked in gold inventory, price-taker dynamics, and zero brand pricing power at this scale. Without evidence of durable EBIT growth or improving capital efficiency, the cheapness is a value trap. The Magic Formula's entire premise — buy good businesses at bargain prices — is violated here because Manoj is simply not a good business. Pass, and redirect screening capital toward the 30-50 Indian mid-caps where ROIC >20% coincides with EBIT/EV >12%.
